//: The machine-checkable half of docs/limitations.md's '## Known divergences' section (chtypes#185). The prose is authored there; this file carries only what the retired v0 checker could drive against loaded artifacts. Every '###' heading under that section must have exactly one entry here (by 'heading', matched verbatim, prefix stripped) and every entry here must match a heading — the retired v0 checker's coverage rule required either side to exist only with the other. Each check's 'settings' are a compile-time profile (a type gate binds at compile, docs/guides/settings.md 'The one exception'); 'err_code' and 'err_msg' are asserted only where docs/limitations.md itself states them — a code without a quoted message means the page named the code alone. 'stored' asserts THIS LIBRARY's current answer for a row's stored text (BatchResult.rows[i].values[column].text) — it is expected to start FAILING the day a relink makes the library match the server, which is the retirement signal for that entry, not a regression. 'stored_same' asserts that several named rows all store IDENTICAL text for a column, with no fixed text of its own — the shape a value computed once (rather than per row or per insert) produces, for a value (a random DEFAULT's exact bytes) that is not reproducible across processes. A check's top-level 'batches' (default 1) drives its payload through its compiled schema that many times, concatenating rows across calls in order, to reproduce separate INSERTs rather than one larger one. A check naming a top-level 'filter' (a boolean SQL expression) is driven down a DIFFERENT call tree: the schema compiles, the filter compiles over it, then Filter.rows(format, payload) answers one Verdict per row ('t'/'f'/'e'/'d') rather than an Outcome — its 'expect' still names 'outcome' (the call-level FilterOutcome, 'ok' unless the call itself was refused) and may also name 'verdicts' (the per-row list, index-aligned with the payload's rows, asserting THIS LIBRARY's current per-row answer exactly as 'stored' asserts a stored value — expected to start FAILING the day a relink makes the library refuse the query instead, the retirement signal for that entry). A check's 'lines' may be narrower than every served line a divergence is measured on: it names the lines THIS CHECK drives, which — like the demangle entry above — is the set where a library fix is expected to land and retire the entry; docs/limitations.md states the full measured scope in prose.

entries.heading: A DEFAULT over demangle admits what a real server refuses to create

checks.note: the divergence itself, on the two served-unsupported lines that got no build at the relink below: allow_introspection_functions defaults to disabled, and a real server refuses the CREATE TABLE with 446 (FUNCTION_NOT_ALLOWED) at that default; this library never consults the setting, so it compiles the schema and stores demangle's answer regardless (server half measured by the artifact producer, not here). On every supported line (26.3, 26.7, 26.8, 26.9) the artifact producer's relink at build 1790845279 made this library refuse the same CREATE TABLE with 446 too, so the divergence no longer reproduces there; this check narrowed to the two lines where it still does
checks.schema: s String, v String DEFAULT demangle(s)

entries.heading: A filter whose result is not a boolean-context type admits rows a real server refuses

checks.note: a filter whose top-level result is Date (not a boolean-context type) answers 't' for every row whose underlying value is non-zero, rather than refusing the query the way a real server does (code 59, ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_COLUMN_FOR_FILTER, at analysis). Measured by the artifact producer on all 12 served lines; scoped here to the four SUPPORTED lines, where a library fix is expected to land — docs/limitations.md has the full line-by-line picture, including the wider admit on 24.8/25.3/25.8 and the float over-hide from 25.10 on. Row 0 and row 2 hold the zero date (1970-01-01); row 1 and row 3 hold a non-zero date
checks.schema: d Date, i128 Int128, e8 Enum8('z' = 0, 'a' = 1), u8 UInt8

checks.note: same over-admit as filter-date-over-admit, over Int128 (also not a boolean-context type): row 0 and row 3 hold 0, rows 1 and 2 hold a non-zero value. Measured by the artifact producer on all 12 served lines; scoped here the same way
checks.schema: d Date, i128 Int128, e8 Enum8('z' = 0, 'a' = 1), u8 UInt8

checks.note: same over-admit as filter-date-over-admit, over Enum8 (also not a boolean-context type): row 0 and row 3 hold the enum's zero value 'z', rows 1 and 2 hold the non-zero value 'a'. Measured by the artifact producer on all 12 served lines; scoped here the same way
checks.schema: d Date, i128 Int128, e8 Enum8('z' = 0, 'a' = 1), u8 UInt8

entries.heading: A CHECK constraint admits any non-zero or non-UInt8 result a real server refuses

checks.note: a CHECK expression on a UInt8 column with a non-zero, non-one result is admitted here; a real server passes a row only when the CHECK result byte equals 1, and rejects this one with code 469. Measured by the artifact producer identically on all 12 served lines; scoped here to the four SUPPORTED lines, where a library fix is expected to land
checks.schema: x UInt8, CONSTRAINT c CHECK x

checks.note: a CHECK expression whose own type is not UInt8 (here Int64) is admitted here; a real server rejects every row with code 1 ('does not return a value of type UInt8'), whatever the value. Measured by the artifact producer identically on all 12 served lines; scoped here the same way
checks.schema: x Int64, CONSTRAINT c CHECK x
